meta.note: China monetary & liquidity seed dataset. Built entirely from files fetched from GitHub in this session - the sandbox egress proxy blocks every macro data host (FRED, NBS, PBoC, ChinaBond, CFETS, BIS, IMF, World Bank) and the WebSearch budget was already exhausted, so no primary-publisher domain could be reached. Two source families: (1) openecon-data, a curated China macro snapshot (AS_OF 2026-07-19) mirroring PBoC/NBS releases via the EastMoney datacenter; (2) the full quarterly text of the PBoC 货币政策执行报告 (Monetary Policy Report) 2018Q1-2026Q1, from which quarterly figures were extracted verbatim by regex - that family is primary-source wording, mirrored. Integrity checks that passed: the LPR change history reproduces the published record exactly; M2, CPI, PPI, TSF-stock YoY and GDP growth agree across two independent mirrors on every overlapping point; the MPR's own stated period-on-period deltas reconcile with its excess-reserve levels. No value in this file was estimated, interpolated or recalled from memory. Series that could not be verified are omitted and listed in gaps rather than filled. Step series (rrr_large, rrr_small) are change-dates-only and meant to be forward-filled; read their notes first, as both are deliberately truncated. Daily-derived series (dr007, cgb_10y) are monthly AVERAGES - see each notes field for the convention.
gaps: omo_7d (7-day reverse repo policy rate): OMITTED. No complete verified step series obtainable. Verified anchors only, from PBoC MPR text: 2.55% through 2019-Q1..2019-Q3; 1.50% at 2025-03; 'cut from 1.5% to 1.4%' during 2025-Q4; 1.40% at 2026-03. Forward-filling four anchors across 2019-2026 would inject wrong levels for every intervening cut (2020, 2022, 2023, 2024), so no series is emitted.

mlf_1y (1-year MLF rate): OMITTED. Same reason - the MPR text describes MLF changes qualitatively ('down 20bp', 'down 30bp') without a dated level series, and no machine-readable source was reachable.
r007: no verified data at any frequency.
ncd_1y_aaa (1-year AAA NCD): not obtainable. ncd_issuance_war (all-tenor weighted average issuance rate, quarterly) is supplied as a directional proxy ONLY and is a different, lower-level measure.
cgb_1y (1-year CGB yield): no verified data. Only the 10Y point of the ChinaBond curve was reachable.
usd_cny monthly average: no verified series. One spot value only - 6.7811 on 2026-08-28 from a fetched dashboard summary - which is not enough to emit a series.
gdp_deflator_yoy: not emitted. Deriving it needs nominal and real growth for the SAME periods; only 7 sparse nominal LEVEL points were verified, so any deflator path would be largely interpolated.
nominal_gdp_yoy: not emitted as a series for the same reason; use nominal_gdp_level_cum and difference it yourself, accepting the NBS revision caveat.
government bond net issuance / fiscal deposits change: no verified data.
dr007: ends 2024-12; no verified 2025-2026 monthly observations.
cgb_10y: starts 2024-08 only; no verified history back to 2015 or 2019.

tsf_stock_yoy / tsf_stock_level / walr_general / excess_reserve_ratio / core_cpi_yoy / ncd_issuance_war are QUARTERLY, because their only verified source is the quarterly PBoC Monetary Policy Report. Monthly TSF-stock YoY was not obtainable.
rrr_large / rrr_small truncated to 2022-04-25..2025-05-15; the source's 2019 and 2021 change dates are missing, so earlier points were withheld rather than forward-filled incorrectly.
tsf_flow ends 2026-04 (MOFCOM republication lag), while monthly PBoC/NBS series run to 2026-06.
core_cpi_yoy is 5 quarterly observations only; no monthly core CPI was obtainable.

ENVIRONMENT CONSTRAINT: the egress proxy 403s every external data host (FRED, NBS, PBoC, ChinaBond, CFETS, BIS, IMF, World Bank, EastMoney, akshare's upstreams), and the WebSearch budget was exhausted before this task began. Only github.com/raw.githubusercontent.com and PyPI were reachable, so EVERY value here came from a file fetched from GitHub. Nothing was fetched from a primary publisher's own domain.
meta.validated: 2026-09-13: 178 observation-level comparisons in research/07-data-validation.md; 175 matched, 3 definitional mismatches. Confidence ratings below reflect that audit.

core_cpi_yoy.notes: SPARSE. Only the quarters where the PBoC MPR states an unambiguous China core-CPI rate for that quarter are included. Deliberately EXCLUDED: 2023Q1/2023Q2 mentions of 5.5-5.6%/4.8%, which are advanced-economy (US) core inflation in the MPR's international section, not China; and full-year averages quoted in Q4 reports (2022: 0.9, 2024: 0.5, 2025: 0.7), which are annual not quarterly. Monthly core CPI was not obtainable. MISLABELLED PERIODS — 3 of 5 points are year-to-date cumulative averages presented as single quarters; 2024-Q3 overstates by about 0.25pp. Directional use only (note 07).

excess_reserve_ratio.notes: Quarter-end ratio quoted verbatim in each PBoC MPR ('X月末，金融机构超额（存款）准备金率为N%'). Complete 2018-Q1..2026-Q1. ncd_issuance_war.name: 3-month NCD issuance rate

ncd_issuance_war.notes: NOT the requested 1-year AAA NCD rate. This is the all-tenor, all-issuer weighted average NCD ISSUANCE rate quoted in the PBoC MPR, and it sits below a 1Y AAA secondary yield because short tenors dominate issuance. Use it as a directional proxy only; do not substitute it for ncd_1y_aaa in a level-sensitive spread. Quarterly only. CORRECTED: this is the 3-MONTH NCD rate, not an all-tenor weighted average as originally labelled. Values verified 14/14 against the PBoC MPR corpus (note 07).

rrr_large.name_zh: 大型金融机构存款准备金率

provenance.source_name: lightfor.github.io economic chart dataset, stated as cross-checked against PBoC announcements

rrr_large.notes: CHANGE DATES ONLY - forward-fill between them. DELIBERATELY TRUNCATED to start 2022-04-25. The source's earlier points are an INCOMPLETE step history: it jumps 2018-10-15 (14.5) straight to 2020-03-16 (13.0), omitting the 2019 cuts, and 2020-03-16 straight to 2022-04-25, omitting the 2021 cuts. Forward-filling those would inject wrong levels across 2019-2021, so they are withheld. Changes after 2025-05-15 are unverified; the 2025Q4 MPR refers to a 0.5pp RRR cut that could not be unambiguously dated.

real_gdp_yoy_cum.name: Real GDP, cumulative YTD YoY %

provenance.source_name: openecon-data (China macro snapshot, AS_OF 2026-07-19); upstream EastMoney datacenter mirror of PBoC / NBS releases

real_gdp_yoy_cum.notes: CUMULATIVE year-to-date growth as released by NBS (Q1 = Q1; Q2 = H1; Q3 = first three quarters; Q4 = full year) - NOT single-quarter growth. Cross-checked against the PBoC MPR, which quotes 5.4 (2025 Q1), 5.3 (2025 H1), 5.2 (2025 Q1-Q3), 5.0 (2025 full year), 5.0 (2026 Q1) - exact match. Matched NBS quarterly releases (note 07).

real_gdp_yoy_q.name: Real GDP, single-quarter YoY %

provenance.source_name: lightfor.github.io economic chart dataset, sourced to NBS

real_gdp_yoy_q.notes: SPARSE - single-quarter (not cumulative) YoY, only available from 2025-Q1 in the source. Arithmetically consistent with real_gdp_yoy_cum.

nominal_gdp_level_cum.name: Nominal GDP, cumulative YTD level (current prices)
nominal_gdp_level_cum.name_zh: 国内生产总值（现价，累计）

provenance.source_name: PBoC 中国货币政策执行报告 (Monetary Policy Report) quarterly full text, 2018Q1-2026Q1, mirrored as cleaned text

nominal_gdp_level_cum.notes: CUMULATIVE year-to-date current-price GDP as quoted in the PBoC MPR in 万亿元, converted to RMB bn (x1000). Q4 entries are FULL-YEAR totals. To get a single-quarter level, difference within a year (e.g. 2025-Q2 = 66100 - 31900 = 34200); to get a 4-quarter rolling sum, use the Q4 full-year figures or chain differences. SPARSE: only 7 points, because most MPRs quote the growth rate without the level. NBS revises these levels, so a YoY computed from two published cumulative levels will not exactly equal the official nominal growth rate. MIXED VINTAGE — do not compute growth across the 2023/24 seam. 2023 = 126,100 is the PRE-census figure (superseded by 129,427.2) while 2024 = 134,900 is preliminary (final 134,806.6). Nominal 2024 growth computes to +7.0% against a true +4.2% — a 2.8pp phantom jump that would corrupt any velocity or credit-to-GDP term. This is why no GDP deflator or nominal growth rate is derived in this build (note 07).
